name: Michaiah
overview: The name Michaiah appears in Scripture as associated with several individuals who served important roles in the religious and civic life of Judah. One Michaiah is noted as the father of Achbor, who was involved in the king's court (2 Kings 22:12). Another Michaiah was a prince sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the law in the cities of Judah, demonstrating a commitment to instructing the people in God's Word (2 Chronicles 17:7). Additionally, Michaiah is identified as a priest from the family of Asaph, participating in temple worship with trumpets (Nehemiah 12:35, 41). Finally, Michaiah the son of Gemariah, a descendant of Shaphan, is recorded as expounding the prophecies of Jeremiah to the princes after they were read by Baruch, underscoring the role of faithful teaching and interpretation of God's revelation to the leaders of Judah (Jeremiah 36:11-12). These references collectively highlight Michaiah as a figure connected to faithful service, teaching, and the transmission of God's Word in different capacities within the Old Testament community.
